driveParameters.customArtifactFrameCount: different: streaming-comparison.json records 9 render snapshots per leg, so the two documents describe different drives and neither supersedes the other
driveParameters.pinnedRedirectRequired: PROBE_PINNED_REDIRECT_FILE is NOT optional for a source the frontend marks proxy:false. Without it run-against-pinned.mjs installs no transport redirect hook, the pinned server fetches the REAL provider, and the peer log stays EMPTY -- which reads exactly like a product hang or a product defect, and did for two rounds here. The seam named in seamEnvVar aims the GoTavern leg and the redirect aims the pinned leg; both are required, and proxyPasswordPresent false on BOTH legs is the evidence that neither leg could have reached a peer through a reverse proxy instead.
driveParameters.peerKeying: the scripted mock provider matches POSITIONALLY and fails in BOTH directions, so the COUNT of model-list answers is not the axis: with ONE entry the pinned generate never arrives (the second status call consumes it and the send is refused with online_status no_connection); with THREE the generate arrives but receives a MODELS body and renders an empty string while the other leg renders text -- an equal-empty that finalTextNonEmpty exists to catch. This drive therefore uses a peer that answers by REQUEST (GET -> model list every time, completion POST -> completion, SSE when streaming and JSON when not), which is correct for any number of status calls.

notes: The probe previously awaited response.clone().text() for EVERY response before returning it to the frontend, so a streamed generate response was fully buffered before the fetch promise resolved: incremental rendering was impossible to observe and an aborted stream observed an empty message. That was a probe defect on both legs (rule 10), fixed by skipping the clone read for text/event-stream and for the generate route. Earlier captures in this directory were taken with that defect; these captures are not.
The peer records clientDisconnected only when the caller closes before the scripted stream finishes; it is the provider-side proof of cancellation.
framesWritten in cancellation mode depends on how many paced frames were written before the abort arrived, so it is recorded for information, not asserted.
Pinned emits extra prompt-manager dry generations (visible as duplicate GENERATE_AFTER_DATA dryRun=true entries); they never issue a provider request and are not part of the comparison.
